canonical_summary: Use one shared compiler core for PlanUnit-to-NodeSeed-to-WorkNode-request compilation, with separate Codex bootstrap and native Puppet Master adapters so there is one truth model and two execution surfaces.
negative_constraints: Do not build two unrelated compilers that drift.

canonical_summary: The Plans-to-work process must be designed so a low-quality, low-context agent can execute or resume each step without remembering the whole project.
negative_constraints: Do not rely on chat memory or one high-context model remembering the full process.

canonical_summary: Define PlanCompileRun as a durable, idempotent, resumable state machine with current_state, stage cards, worklists, waves, source hashes, currentness gates, exact NEXT routing, blockers, receipts, and resume actions.
negative_constraints: Do not implement PlanCompile as a giant prompt chain.

canonical_summary: PlanCompile stages should include preflight/currentness, scope selection, PlanUnit normalization, dependency/cycle analysis, surface mapping, work type and effort classification, NodeSeed candidate synthesis, split/merge sizing, NodeSeed review, WorkGraph draft, WorkNode request emission, adapter emission, and certification/handoff.
Each PlanCompile stage must have a tiny contract listing purpose, read files, write files, forbidden writes, entry gate, item bounds, exit gate, success route, and blocked route.
negative_constraints: Do not ask an agent to reason over the full Plan index when a bounded worklist can be used.

canonical_summary: PlanCompile runtime must remain disabled/design-only until a later explicit enablement PlanUnit or feature flag is accepted.
negative_constraints: Do not create production WorkNodes, executable WorkGraphs, dispatched GoalRuns, or native queues in this phase.

canonical_summary: Plan Compile specifically means converting approved Plans/PlanUnits into NodeSeeds, WorkGraph drafts, and WorkNode requests. It does not mean executing WorkNodes or producing code.
negative_constraints: Do not show Executor code-generation progress inside the Plan Compile tab except final handoff status.

canonical_summary: Use Plan Wizard terminology going forward in new records, prompts, and plan updates.
negative_constraints: Do not introduce new references or meta-comments using the old Chain Wizard name.

canonical_summary: After runtime enablement, Plan Wizard approval should automatically and invisibly start native PlanCompile, create a compile run, and project progress in Orchestrator.
negative_constraints: Do not enable this automatic launch yet.

canonical_summary: The Codex side should be startable from one goal prompt, write durable artifacts under a compile directory, support resume by compile_id, and produce Codex work packages rather than native runtime dispatch.
negative_constraints: Do not depend on the native Puppet Master scheduler for bootstrap.

canonical_summary: Codex bootstrap may emit external GUI-agent CLI request artifacts for GUI/frontend work using Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, or custom CLI providers, with Codex parent verification.
negative_constraints: Do not expose this bridge as a built Puppet Master setting.

canonical_summary: Native Puppet Master must route GUI/frontend WorkNodes through configured native provider/model capability lanes, not through Codex-specific external GUI-agent CLI settings.
negative_constraints: No Antigravity/Claude Code/Cursor/OpenCode CLI bridge setting in built Puppet Master.

canonical_summary: NodeSeed candidates are non-executable intermediate artifacts carrying source PlanUnit IDs, objective, owner area, surfaces, acceptance, validators, dependency refs, risk, reasoning tier, work type, effort, GUI flag, capability requirements, authority policy, sizing, status, and blockers.
negative_constraints: Do not treat NodeSeeds as final WorkNodes.

canonical_summary: A NodeSeed review gate must prove coverage, excluded dispositions, acceptance criteria, validators or explicit gaps, bounded write surfaces, dependencies, GUI flags, risk/reasoning/capability metadata, and absence of executable WorkNodes.

WorkGraph draft is the first executable-shaped artifact but remains reviewable before dispatch; it carries nodes, entrypoints, dependency edges, scheduler policy, graph integrity, authority, evidence, and validation state.
negative_constraints: Do not dispatch from WorkGraph draft before certified Executor intake.

canonical_summary: PlanCompile emits WorkNode requests, not runnable WorkNodes. Executor intake must validate and accept them before dispatch.
negative_constraints: Do not let PlanCompile directly dispatch worker execution.

canonical_summary: Every NodeSeed/WorkNode request needs work_type, gui_related, frontend_related, effort class, reasoning tier, context size, validation cost, risk class, authority risk, user-visible risk, and capability lane metadata.
User-facing model settings should be Default Model, Overseer Model, Worker Model, GUI / Frontend Worker Model, High-Effort Worker Model, and Auditor Model.
negative_constraints: Do not expose a long list of internal subrole settings.

canonical_summary: Default Model covers assistant chat, normal Plan Wizard conversation, ordinary research/browser lookup, and default fallback behavior.

Overseer Model covers Plan Wizard ledger-to-Plans conversion, PRD Builder structured conversion, Plans-to-WorkNode-request compilation, seam/split/merge decisions, execution supervision, graph patch recommendations, and blocked-state reasoning.
negative_constraints: Do not create a separate user-facing Plan Compiler Model unless later added as advanced override.

canonical_summary: Worker Model handles normal WorkNode implementation; GUI / Frontend Worker Model handles GUI/frontend/UX/layout/visual WorkNodes; High-Effort Worker Model handles difficult, broad, repo-wide, high-risk, or high-reasoning WorkNodes.
Auditor Model replaces old Plan Wizard validation pass model settings and owns audit/repair/audit loops, verification, certification, quality gates, and evidence review.
negative_constraints: Do not keep fixed Pass 1 / Pass 2 / Pass 3 Plan Wizard model settings.

canonical_summary: Executor should not have a user-facing model setting because Executor is deterministic scheduler/runtime machinery. Overseer handles execution-level reasoning around Executor.
negative_constraints: Do not call the deterministic scheduler a model-backed Executor agent.

canonical_summary: Every dispatched WorkNode must record requested lane, requested model/profile, effective model/profile, fallback used, fallback reason, and capability checks.

WorkNode requests must include ordering metadata: build_phase, dependency_type, depends_on, unblocks, parallel_group_id, scheduler_lane, manual_priority, ordering_reason, and required before/after start/completion relationships.

Default build order should begin with test capability discovery, source-control/worktree/safe-point discovery, environment/toolchain setup, contracts/schemas/storage, core runtime/execution, providers/models/settings/permissions, GUI shell/navigation, features, integration/seams, automated tests/browser/device checks, source-control promotion, and final Auditor certification.

Create or update a first-class Automated Testing System that owns test capability discovery, harness probing, test strategy generation, WorkNode test binding, test run receipts, visual/browser/emulator evidence, platform adapters, fallback and blocker policy.
negative_constraints: Do not treat tests as a thin verificationCommand afterthought.

canonical_summary: Before test generation or execution, Puppet Master should detect project platform, framework/toolkit, local tools, app launch ability, browser/GUI/device/emulator automation, screenshots, logs, headless/headed support, project-native test runners, and when needed research official/current testing options.
WorkNode completion cannot require human eyeballing. Tests, smoke checks, app launch, browser/GUI/device sessions, screenshots, logs, and evidence capture must run automatically where required.
negative_constraints: Do not make manual visual inspection a required completion step.

canonical_summary: Slint live preview/live reload is relevant to building Puppet Master itself, but testing must be platform-capability-discovery-first and not overfit to Slint because most users will not be building Slint apps.
negative_constraints: Do not hyper-focus automated testing around Slint.

canonical_summary: For web projects, once Puppet Master is built, Puppet Master built-in browser automation should be the primary web test automation path; Playwright can be optional/fallback/project-native, not the native default.
negative_constraints: Do not default native Puppet Master web testing to Playwright when the built-in browser can do it.

canonical_summary: Automated tests need project-type-specific oracles: browser DOM/console/network/screenshot/visual checks, desktop GUI launch/window/screenshot/accessibility, mobile emulator/device logs/screenshots, backend API/contract/database checks, CLI exit/output/filesystem checks, and library unit/property/API contracts.

Each WorkNode request must carry test_binding fields: required capabilities, required harnesses, generated/reused tests, completion commands, browser/session requirements, emulator requirements, visual evidence requirements, and test_gap_policy.
If the system cannot verify a WorkNode automatically, it must create a test capability blocker or test-harness WorkNode rather than silently passing.
negative_constraints: Do not silently allow unverifiable WorkNodes.

canonical_summary: Source control, worktrees, snapshots, safe points, rollback, FileSafe, and GitHub belong to the execution flow after WorkNode requests are accepted by Executor, not to PlanCompile itself.
negative_constraints: Do not make PlanCompile own source-control mutation.

canonical_summary: Mutation-capable WorkNode attempts must run in known repo/worktree context; parallel WorkNodes need isolated worktrees or explicit clean allocation; dirty, conflicted, contaminated, blocked-preserved, lineage-mismatched worktrees cannot be reused silently.
Mutation-capable attempts must create or verify a safe point before risky execution, support restore_safe_point_then_retry where required, and record rollback availability in receipts.
GitHub should handle auth, remote state, push, PRs, PR status, and GitHub Actions only when configured; local source-control/worktree state remains execution truth.
negative_constraints: Do not require GitHub for local-only project completion.

canonical_summary: Execution should emit source_control_preflight_receipt, safe_point_receipt, worknode_change_receipt, merge_or_promotion_receipt, and source-control finalization receipt with repo/worktree/branch/baseline/head/safe point/changed files/conflicts/rollback fields.

Each WorkNode execution should produce dispatch, source-control preflight, safe point, change, test run, Auditor verification, repair attempt if needed, merge/promotion if applicable, and completion receipts.

Add a handoff matrix proving every transition from Plan Wizard approval through PlanCompile, Executor intake, source-control preflight, dispatch, tests, Auditor verification, repair, promotion, graph completion, and certification has source artifact, destination artifact, owner, validator, receipt, retry route, rollback route, and user-escalation condition.
WorkNode requests become runnable only after Executor intake validates graph integrity, source-control/test/model/authority requirements, readiness prerequisites, and scheduler metadata.
negative_constraints: Do not let WorkNodeRequest bypass Executor intake.

canonical_summary: Code completion means all WorkNodes terminal with valid receipts, all required automated tests passed or explicitly dispositioned, all source-control receipts valid, rollback/safe-point requirements satisfied, Auditor passed, no active blockers, no stale Plan/WorkGraph/currentness mismatch, final source state clean or intentionally preserved, and final summary/evidence written.
negative_constraints: Do not accept worker says done as code completion.

canonical_summary: Default mode is hands-off and user escalation is last-resort for critical authority blockers. HITL is an explicit setting/mode that may add configured package/seam/critical checkpoints without becoming required for correctness.
negative_constraints: Do not ask the user for ordinary row-level uncertainty in default mode.

canonical_summary: Default user escalation should be limited to missing credentials/secrets, billing/payment/legal/license acceptance, unsafe destructive operation, irreversible external side effect, unrecoverable environment failure, true product decision with no inferable answer, or security-sensitive approval.

Repeated failures should escalate from normal repair to Auditor failure-signature classification, Overseer graph/work/model/source-control/test-harness repair, High-Effort/Auditor deep repair, and only then critical user escalation unless HITL policy says otherwise.
negative_constraints: Do not jump to user decision because a low-quality agent got stuck.

canonical_summary: Repair loops need failure signatures with kind, normalized_key, attempt_count, last_safe_point_id, last_repair_worknode_id, Overseer/Auditor reviewed flags, repeated failure policy, and escalation lane.

If Plans change while execution is underway, affected lanes should pause, a PlanDiffImpactReport should classify nodes as unaffected, needs_recompile, invalidated, or already_safe, then patch WorkGraph or create replan WorkNodes before resuming after currentness gates.

Execution must define network access, secret access, filesystem write, destructive command, database/test-data, browser profile isolation, real-account vs sandbox-account, credential redaction, and artifact privacy/retention policies.

Add a dedicated Plan Compile tab to Orchestrator for the long Plans-to-WorkNode creation process, showing stage timeline, current activity, PlanUnits processed, NodeSeeds drafted, WorkNode requests drafted, dependency/seam graph, test capability requirements, model lane routing, GUI/high-effort counts, Auditor loop status, throughput, speed, ETA confidence, blockers, warnings, and handoff readiness.

The Plan Compile tab should be heavily animated, pretty, polished, and engaging: Plans flow into PlanUnits, cards sort into lanes, NodeSeeds assemble, dependency edges draw, GUI/frontend badges appear, test gates light up, WorkNode requests snap into graph clusters, and handoff pulses toward Executor.
negative_constraints: Do not implement Plan Compile as a static JSON/log table.

canonical_summary: The Plan Compile tab shows only the process of converting Plans into nodes/work requests. Executor/Orchestrator code generation progress belongs in existing Progress, Node Graph, Evidence, History, or execution views.
negative_constraints: Do not overload Plan Compile tab with WorkNode execution/code-generation details beyond handoff status.

canonical_summary: Existing Orchestrator execution views should show queued/active/blocked/completed WorkNodes, model lanes, worktrees, safe points, tests, browser/device sessions, repair loops, Auditor status, GitHub PR/Actions if configured, and final certification progress.
Semantic/audit closure registry patterns should be reused so repeated Plan Wizard, PlanCompile, and WorkNode verification findings do not recur when source/canonical evidence has not changed.
Plans-to-code completion must preserve separate source evidence, canonical Plan evidence, process evidence, governance evidence, test evidence, source-control evidence, and completion receipts.

The next step is to record and compile this design into Plans only. Do not build WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, NodeSeed candidates, executable queues, final node manifests, implementation files, production build tasks, or final node queues.
negative_constraints: PlanCompile dry-run/non-executable schema examples may be documented but not emitted as runtime work.

canonical_summary: Add or update schema drafts for PlanCompileRun, stage cards, compile worklists, NodeSeed candidates, NodeSeed review, WorkGraph draft, WorkNode request, compiler model routing, codex work package, codex external GUI-agent request, PlanCompile receipt, automated testing reports, test cases, test run receipts, visual evidence, source-control receipts, model resolution receipts, and goal completion receipts.

Update Plan_To_Node_Compilation, Goal_Runtime_System, Orchestrator_Page, Executor_Protocol, Models_System, FinalGUISpec, Contracts_V0, Project_Output_Artifacts, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel, WorktreeGitImprovement, FileSafe, GitHub docs, Permissions, Tools, Planning_Ledger_System, Plan_Document_System, and 00-plans-index. Add Automated_Testing_System if needed.

After this ledger is compiled to Plans, Codex should run a post-compile audit/index/governance goal that validates the updated Plans, repairs exact-detail drift, regenerates PlanUnit index only after Plans are stable, seals governance if appropriate, and still does not run PlanCompile or build WorkNodes.

The architecture is viable from approved Plans to code completion if every handoff is artifact-backed: PlanCompile emits WorkNode requests, Executor intakes, source-control/test/model/authority preflights run, workers implement, automated tests run, Auditor verifies, repair loops close, source-control promotion happens if configured, and final certification proves completion.

The ledger-to-Plans compile must include implementation-ready PlanUnits and contract details, not only conceptual prose. A structured implementation_readiness_matrix must map each design area to required PlanUnits, schemas, fields, acceptance criteria, validators, owner docs, consumer docs, and no-build boundaries.
negative_constraints: Do not compile vague roadmap prose that leaves future agents to infer the contracts.

canonical_summary: The ledger-to-Plans compile must maintain a doc_impact_matrix listing primary owner docs, direct consumer docs, reference/index/UI docs, search tokens, required update types, deferred rename handling, and per-doc no-update evidence when references are intentionally unchanged.
negative_constraints: Do not update only the obvious owner docs while leaving stale references in consumer/index/UI docs.

canonical_summary: After canonical Plans edits, Codex must run a reference/backlink scan for touched concepts and update direct references, backlinks, index docs, UI command docs, wiring/docs crosswalks, and generated-index inputs or record explicit no-update/deferred evidence.
negative_constraints: Do not claim ledger-to-Plans compile complete until reference scan results are recorded.

canonical_summary: When a PlanUnit changes an owner contract, Codex must update owner prose, then consumer docs and reference/index/UI docs only where they directly reference the changed contract. Broad Plan Wizard rename remains deferred to the Plan Wizard redesign unless a touched section would otherwise introduce stale wording or contradictions.
exact_tokens: broad Plan Wizard rename remains deferred
negative_constraints: Do not do an uncontrolled whole-repo rename as part of this compile; do not leave direct contradictions in touched sections.
